name: UK Ancestry visa

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being a Commonwealth citizen, or holding British Overseas Citizen, British Overseas Territories Citizen, British National (Overseas), or Zimbabwean citizen status.

This requires at least one grandparent born in the UK, the Channel Islands, or the Isle of Man (or before 31 March 1922 in what is now Ireland, or on a UK-registered ship or aircraft). Adoption and unmarried parents/grandparents count; step-parents do not.
This requires being able and planning to work in the UK — no specific job offer is required, but genuine intent to work must be demonstrated.
This must be applied for from outside the UK — there is no in-country switching route onto UK Ancestry, except for former Ancestry visa holders returning.

evidence_required.document: Grandparent's UK/Channel Islands/Isle of Man birth certificate
Full documented ancestry chain (birth/marriage certificates linking applicant to the qualifying grandparent)

outcome.duration_length: 5 years, extendable by a further 5 years

notes: Fee £726 confirmed via gov.uk; secondary sources showing £637/£682 are stale — another clean counterfeit-figure case. Unrestricted work rights from day one (employed, self-employed, or voluntary, full or part-time) — genuinely unusual among sponsored/assessed routes in this dataset, closer to Global Talent's freedom than to a standard work-sponsored route, despite not requiring any endorsement. Confirmed via direct research: UK Ancestry does NOT have its own citizenship pathway — holders naturalise through the standard ILR route (uk_citizenship 'via_ilr_general' group), so citizenship_after_months here reflects the standard 5-year-residence-plus-12-month-ILR-hold total (72 months), not a shortcut. No in-country switching onto this route from any other visa — must apply from outside the UK, a genuine structural difference from most other routes encoded so far.
